papers.title: Real-time detection of N2 and N3 sleep from scalp and intracranial EEG
papers.summary: Developed a causal tracker that estimates N2+N3 sleep every 2 s from the preceding 10 s of scalp or intracranial EEG, achieved near-offline discrimination in epilepsy patients (scalp AUC 0.953; scalp plus thalamus 0.967), and used it to simulate closed-loop stimulation gating. The gating rule permitted stimulation within 5 min in 63-73% of N2+N3 transitions (median delay 42-64 s) but switched on incorrectly 1.4-1.8 times per hour outside N2+N3.

papers.title: Automated Sleep Staging Performance Across Two Experimental Sleep Manipulation Protocols in Adolescents.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: Evaluated POPS, YASA, and combined POPS+YASA automated sleep staging against manual polysomnography in adolescents across a sleep restriction protocol and a slow-wave sleep deprivation protocol. All approaches showed moderate-to-substantial agreement (κ 0.53–0.76), but agreement declined under sleep restriction (poorer Wake, N1, N2 classification) and on the SWSD night (poorer N3 classification).

papers.title: Comprehensive benchmarking of EEG biomarkers for Parkinson's disease: robustness, reliability, and clinical discriminability across multiple datasets.
papers.summary: Benchmarked 16 EEG-derived biomarkers for Parkinson's disease across three independent resting-state datasets, assessing robustness to preprocessing, window length, channel aggregation, and clinical discriminability. Aperiodic, entropy/complexity, and fractal features showed high methodological robustness, whereas oscillatory markers such as beta-gamma phase-amplitude coupling and burst metrics varied substantially across analytical choices.

papers.title: Coverage collapse and deceptive calibration in EEG fatigue monitoring: a cross-dataset audit under within-session and cross-subject shift.
papers.summary: Audited calibration, coverage, and transfer of EEG-based driver fatigue monitors across five model families and three public corpora, showing that pooled calibration error can improve as accuracy degrades and that marginal coverage can mask failure in fatigued states. A derived coverage ceiling and rolling conformal recalibration restored coverage (0.886–0.909) and reduced between-subject coverage variability from 0.205 to 0.026.

papers.title: Detection of Spreading Depolarization with Noninvasive Electroencephalography.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: Developed and validated WAVEFRONT, a noninvasive scalp EEG biomarker of spreading depolarization based on delta-band spatiotemporal propagation, using concurrent scalp EEG and invasive ECoG in patients with TBI, SAH, or malignant hemispheric stroke. Cross-validated detection reached a 97.3% true positive rate at 6.0% false positive rate, and biomarker burden on post-arrest day 3 was greater in cardiac arrest patients with poor neurological outcome.

papers.title: Probing EEG Foundation Model Attention Maps for Lightweight Interpretable Emotion Recognition
papers.summary: Proposed a lightweight, fine-tuning-free approach that aggregates first-layer self-attention weights of the pretrained EEG foundation model REVE into weighted functional-connectivity matrices, using a label-free symmetry criterion to select informative heads. Classifiers on the single best head achieved balanced accuracy and F1 competitive with several fully fine-tuned EEG foundation models on SEED-IV with at least two orders of magnitude fewer computations, and highlighted over-represented frontal connections.

papers.title: Temporal Associations Between Physiological Sleep and Next-Day Pain Intensity in Individuals With Activity-Limiting Chronic Pain: A Multiple Night At-Home Ear-EEG Sleep-Monitoring Study.
papers.summary: Pre-registered prospective observational study (NCT06368531) using at-home ear-EEG across 11-33 nights in 19 individuals with chronic pain to examine night-to-night sleep variability and its temporal association with next-day pain. Lower next-day pain was associated with greater N3 duration, percentage, and stability, whereas higher pain was linked to N3 fragmentation and higher N1 proportion, with ICC values below 0.5 across many sleep metrics.

papers.title: Next generation Human Neocortical Neurosolver model with biophysically realistic somatic, dendritic and synaptic dynamics
papers.summary: Presents a substantially updated Human Neocortical Neurosolver canonical circuit model with electrophysiological and synaptic properties tuned to human tissue, adding L5 ET dendritic Ca2+ spikes and shorter L2/3 dendritic spikes. Demonstrates workflows for disentangling somatic, synaptic, and dendritic contributions to human EEG/MEG event-related responses and oscillations.

papers.title: Disrupted sleep-wake regulation in the MCI-Park mouse model of Parkinson's Disease
papers.summary: Characterized sleep-wake regulation in the MCI-Park progressive mouse model of Parkinson's disease near transition to the parkinsonian state, finding increased wakefulness, reduced NREM and REM sleep, increased sleep fragmentation, and altered EEG activity patterns that mirror PD patient sleep abnormalities.

papers.title: Characterising cortical perturbation-recovery dynamics using TMSEEG: The Brain Dynamic Metric Toolbox
papers.summary: The study adapted dynamical measures from computational perturbation models to TMS-EEG data and applied them to analyze cortical perturbation-recovery dynamics in 16 healthy adults during long-interval intracortical inhibition (LICI). It found that LICI altered the temporal evolution of dynamical measures: Perturbative Integration Latency Index distinguished conditions in the earliest post-stimulation window, Autocorrelation Function Width differences persisted across a broader early interval, and Lyapunov Exponent showed weaker discrimination, demonstrating that extended post-stimulation trajectories reveal additional features of cortical resilience and temporal memory.

papers.title: EEG-based deep learning estimates preterm infants' cerebral age: Contribution of slow-wave and cross-frequency coupling.
papers.summary: Trained a convolutional neural network on spontaneous EEG from 165 healthy preterm infants (28-38 weeks PMA) to predict postmenstrual age, achieving a mean absolute error of 0.75 ± 0.60 weeks with 73.9% of errors within one week. Signal manipulation showed performance depended on low-frequency (<4 Hz) activity and on phase-amplitude coupling before 34 weeks PMA, implicating slow-wave dynamics and cross-frequency coupling as maturation signatures.

papers.title: Electroencephalography-based machine learning models for hyperacute detection of large vessel occlusion stroke.
papers.summary: Assessed EEG-based machine learning models for prehospital detection of anterior circulation large vessel occlusion stroke using 8 dry electrodes in 336 patients with suspected stroke; Naive Bayes achieved the highest AUC (0.85) with 69% sensitivity and 86% specificity. The authors conclude accuracy is moderately high but EEG acquisition must improve before clinical implementation.

papers.title: Developmental interactions between oscillatory and spontaneous neural activity support improvements in inhibitory control from adolescence into adulthood
papers.summary: Used longitudinal EEG from 146 participants (ages 10-34) during an antisaccade task to test how frontal oscillatory and broadband spontaneous activity interact during inhibitory response preparation. Spontaneous activity decreased with development and was linked to lower trial-to-trial latency variability, while age-dependent suppression of preparatory high-beta oscillations became more pronounced with development.

papers.title: Age-specific pediatric templates improve EEG source-reconstructed biomarkers in children
papers.summary: Compared EEG source-reconstructed biomarkers using individual MRI, age-specific pediatric templates (ages 6-17), and the adult fsaverage template in 384 children aged 5.5-17.5 years. Pediatric templates matched individual MRI-based biomarker values more closely than the adult template across power, DFA, and fE/I measures up to about age 12, supporting their use when individual MRI is unavailable.

papers.title: Temporal coupling shapes the effects of prolonged muscle-tendon vibration on sensorimotor EEG activity during motor imagery.
papers.summary: Tested whether 20-minute suprapatellar muscle-tendon vibration (100 Hz) versus SHAM conditioning modulates EEG alpha- and beta-band event-related desynchronization during imagined knee extensions in 20 healthy adults. Post-vibration motor imagery showed reduced alpha and beta ERD, while imagery concurrent with vibration selectively increased alpha ERD, indicating state-dependent effects of prolonged proprioceptive conditioning on sensorimotor cortical engagement.

papers.title: Participant-Disjoint EEG Decoding of Instructed Respiratory Conditions Using a Deep Spatio-Respiratory Transformer.
papers.journal: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
papers.summary: Developed a Deep Spatio-Respiratory Transformer (DSRT) using differential entropy and normalized power-ratio EEG features with a four-layer Transformer encoder for eight-class instructed respiratory-condition decoding, achieving participant-level accuracy of 0.7429 ± 0.0492 and improving over EEG Conformer by 3.78 accuracy points.

papers.title: Mental-Fatigue-Related Changes in EEG Microstate Dynamics and Microstate-Conditioned Phase-Amplitude Coupling.
papers.summary: Analyzed EEG microstate temporal dynamics and microstate C-conditioned theta/alpha-to-beta phase-amplitude coupling across mental fatigue levels during a simulated-flight task. High fatigue was associated with shorter duration, lower occurrence, and lower time coverage of microstate C, plus elevated theta-beta and alpha-beta PAC in frontal and parietal regions.

papers.title: Feedback Valence, Prediction Error, and the Limits of Computational Attribution in Symptom-Related EEG
papers.summary: Re-analyzed an anxiety-related feedback-locked EEG association across two open probabilistic-learning datasets, finding greater trait anxiety linked to larger negative-minus-positive FCz theta responses but no established theta specificity. Feedback valence and signed prediction error were nearly collinear (r=-0.964), and signed PE added only limited held-out predictive value beyond valence, constraining computational attribution at the individual level.

papers.title: Human iEEG recordings during audiovisual speech violations support and extend predictive routing models.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Used human intracranial EEG in seven presurgical epilepsy patients during an audiovisual speech paradigm to test predictive routing models of gamma and alpha-beta oscillations. Auditory deviance and McGurk-incongruent conditions showed increased high-gamma and decreased alpha-beta power in superior temporal cortex, while frontal areas showed a theta-band prediction error signal.

papers.title: Developmental trajectories of pain empathy: evidence from drift diffusion modeling and EEG time-frequency analysis.
papers.summary: Examined pain empathy development in 120 children, adolescents, and adults using an attention-to-pain-cue task with hierarchical drift-diffusion modeling and EEG time-frequency analysis. Children showed lower drift rates, wider decision boundaries, and longer non-decision times, and EEG revealed reduced alpha/beta event-related desynchronization differentiation between painful and non-painful stimuli when pain cues were task-irrelevant.

papers.title: Structural and EEG Motor Networks Distinguish Level of Motor Impairment After Stroke.
papers.summary: Combined MRI-derived structural connectivity and source-localized EEG functional connectivity to distinguish high versus low upper-extremity motor impairment after stroke. Structural disconnection of brainstem from M1 and PMd predicted low motor status, and high-function patients showed stronger delta ipsilesional and beta contralesional connectivity and more efficient local network organization.

papers.title: Opposing effects of childhood abuse and neglect on neural performance monitoring.
papers.summary: Tested the dimensional model of adversity in 782 young adults using the Childhood Trauma Questionnaire and an Eriksen flanker EEG task. Abuse was associated with enhanced error-related negativity, whereas neglect was associated with attenuated ERN and reduced frontal midline theta, with stronger effects in males.

papers.title: Transforming neurophysiological data into measurable stress metric using machine learning-based stress quantification framework for smart factory workers.
papers.summary: Proposed and tested an integrated framework combining EEG, fNIRS, gaze tracking, and machine learning for continuous mental stress estimation in smart factory workers. Ensemble models using STAI scores as target achieved 84.1% classification accuracy and RMSE 10.86 for regression, with behavioral and subjective measures reflecting process-variable effects.

papers.title: Spectral power and functional connectivity of resting EEG in people exposed to armed conflict and controls.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: Compared resting-state EEG spectral power and weighted phase lag index connectivity between 74 Colombian adults exposed to armed conflict and 48 controls. Median occipital and global alpha power and temporal theta relative power were lower in exposed participants, but no spectral or connectivity contrast survived correction across 78 EEG tests.

papers.title: Mirror Neural System in Hands Motor Imagery with Pictures and Videos Guidance: An EEG-fNIRS Study.
papers.journal: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
papers.summary: Compared EEG-fNIRS cortical activation across motor execution, motor imagery, picture-guided and video-guided motor imagery, finding that guided motor imagery reliably recruits mirror neurons during imagination despite not easing task difficulty according to participant feedback.

papers.title: Generative-augmented multimodal neuroaffective decoding for product evaluation: toward neurofeedback-driven human-in-the-loop co-design.
papers.summary: Introduces GAMAF, a generative-augmented multimodal fusion model combining cWGAN-GP, cross-modal attention, graph-based interactions, and adaptive weighting to decode perceived attractiveness, innovativeness, and friendliness from EEG, eye tracking, and peripheral signals in 150 participant-stimulus trials. GAMAF reached mean outer-fold R² of 0.810, 0.850, and 0.840, exceeding a Multimodal Transformer baseline and reducing aggregate MAE and RMSE by about 29.6% and 29.7%.

papers.title: Scalable hardware and software for high-density, multi-regional electrophysiology in non-human primates.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present MIND, a lightweight implantable microdrive enabling stable chronic recordings from multiple independently positioned Neuropixels probes, paired with UnitAssay, an automated spike-sorting curation framework. Tested in rhesus macaques across parietal, prefrontal, and motor cortices during reaching and eye-movement tasks, the platform achieved stable multi-probe recordings and improved reliable single-unit identification relative to Kilosort 4 and standard SpikeInterface quality control.

papers.title: Resting-State EEG Spectral Power in Young Adults With Generalized Anxiety Disorder and Self-Reported Habitual Short Sleep: A Case-Control Study.
papers.summary: This exploratory case-control study compared resting-state EEG spectral power in 28 young adults with generalized anxiety disorder and self-reported habitual short sleep versus 28 healthy controls. After age and sex adjustment no whole-scalp frequency-band comparison survived FDR correction, but exploratory channel-wise analyses showed higher delta and theta power concentrated over posterior and centroparietal electrodes.

papers.title: Electric and Magnetic Source Imaging in Epilepsy: Anatomical Insights from Realistic Simulations
papers.summary: Used realistic simulations with known ground-truth cortical, insular, and hippocampal sources from patient-derived intracranial EEG spike waveforms to compare HD-EEG, MEG, and combined electromagnetic source imaging. EEG showed higher spike sensitivity for radial gyral-crown and sulcal-bottom sources, MEG for tangential sulcal-wall sources, and dipole scanning localized cortical and insular sources more accurately than dSPM or LCMV; combined EMSI outperformed ESI but not MSI.

papers.title: Different modes of stimulation at the Neiguan acupoint (PC6) regulate different EEG microstates under VR immersion conditions.
papers.summary: In 200 healthy participants randomized to control, 40 °C, 44 °C, or 2-Hz TEAS stimulation at the PC6 acupoint under VR immersion, EEG microstate analysis showed that 2-Hz TEAS increased duration, occurrence, and coverage of microstate D during stimulation, while thermal and electrical modalities engaged distinct microstate changes. Findings indicate that different PC6 stimulation modes modulate VR motion sickness through partially distinct central pathways reflected in microstates A, B, and D.

papers.title: Decoding and Characterizing the Intracranial Representation of Semantic Information
papers.summary: Using intracranial sEEG high-gamma power during language tasks in epilepsy patients, the authors trained supervised classifiers on trial-level features and decoded semantic category information significantly above chance, reaching 29.8% mean accuracy across 15 categories (chance 6.7%). This demonstrates that conceptual category membership is accessible on individual trials from intracranial population recordings.

papers.title: Integrating uncertainty and practice variability for epilepsy prognostication after intracranial EEG: A meta-analysis.
papers.summary: Meta-analysis of 115 studies of epilepsy surgery after intracranial EEG found that 67% of patients proceeded to resection, 52% achieved seizure freedom, and 58% had a favorable outcome; individual patient-level models identified lesional MRI and cortical malformation as predictors of favorable outcome and bilateral implantation as predictive of less favorable outcome. The models were well calibrated but showed only modest discrimination.

papers.title: Neuromodulatory effects of audio-proprio-phonatory reinforcement training on subjective tinnitus, a HD-EEG study protocol.
papers.summary: Presents a protocol for a prospective, block-randomized, controlled two-arm trial evaluating audio-proprio-phonatory reinforcement training in 56 patients with chronic subjective tinnitus, with the Tinnitus Handicap Inventory as primary endpoint. HD-EEG before and after Phase 1 will assess intervention-related changes in brain activity such as functional connectivity.

papers.title: Advancing Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation for Depression: Novel Protocols, Precision Targeting, and Future Directions.
papers.summary: This expert opinion reviews recent advances in repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) for depression, covering novel protocols such as theta-burst stimulation, accelerated and priming regimens, MRI-guided targeting, and closed-loop systems using real-time EEG or fNIRS feedback. It discusses challenges including cost, standardization, and technical barriers, and outlines future directions for improving rTMS efficiency, precision, and accessibility.

papers.title: Yield of epileptiform abnormalities and predictors on routine electroencephalography in a neurology facility in Ghana.
papers.summary: In a retrospective analysis of 124 patients who underwent routine outpatient EEG at a Ghanaian tertiary center, epileptiform discharges were found in 72 patients (58.1% yield), with generalized epilepsy accounting for 83.3% of abnormalities. Abnormal EEG background activity was the only independent predictor of epileptiform discharges (aOR = 23.47, 95% CI: 2.95–186.86, p = 0.003).

papers.title: Impairment of ictal consciousness and psychosis in drug-resistant focal epilepsy: A retrospective clinical cohort study.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 232 seizures from adults with drug-resistant focal epilepsy, the probability of psychosis of epilepsy peaked at intermediate scores on the Consciousness Seizure Scale (GEE, OR = 4.31, p = .006), independent of epilepsy and seizure duration. The findings suggest that partial disruption of ictal awareness may favor the emergence of psychotic symptoms.

papers.title: Assessing the Effectiveness, Engagement, and Acceptability of a Smartwatch Healthy Lifestyle Intervention for Cognitive Enhancement in Healthy Adults: Mixed Methods Electroencephalography Protocol.
papers.summary: Describes a convergent parallel mixed-methods protocol randomizing 72 sedentary healthy adults to a 4-week Apple Watch lifestyle intervention or standard physical activity guidance. Effectiveness will be assessed via EEG event-related potentials (N2/P3) during a go/no-go task, resting-state EEG spectral power, behavioral performance, perceived health, plus engagement and acceptability measures.

papers.title: The SIK1-NR4A2 axis: a core driver of epilepsy identified by integrated machine learning and experimental validation.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: Integrating machine-learning screening of LKB1 pathway genes in GEO datasets with PTZ-induced status epilepticus rats, AAV knockdown/overexpression, and patch-clamp recording, the study identified SIK1 as a top-ranked epilepsy risk gene that is upregulated in SE hippocampus. SIK1 knockdown prolonged seizure latency and reduced seizure duration, SIK1 negatively regulated NR4A2, and co-overexpression of NR4A2 reversed SIK1's pro-epileptic effect, supporting a SIK1-NR4A2 axis in epilepsy.

papers.title: A mechanistic classification of GNAO1 mutations links Gβγ sequestration to hyperkinetic disease and treatment response.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Combining human genetic analysis with cellular assays, the authors classified GNAO1 variants into those predicted to sequester Gβγ versus those with reduced Gαo expression and increased Gβγ signaling, finding that Gβγ-release-impairing mutations were significantly associated with NEDIM. In GNAO1 R209H/+ mice, caffeine and the Gβγ modulator gallein both reduced hyperlocomotion, and patch-clamp recordings revealed sex- and cell-type-specific hyperexcitability in dorsolateral striatal spiny projection neurons.

papers.title: Rapidly progressive cognitive decline and drug-induced encephalopathy secondary to teprotumumab for thyroid eye disease: a case report and narrative literature review.
papers.summary: This case report and narrative review describes a 56-year-old Han-Chinese man with Graves' disease and thyroid eye disease who developed rapidly progressive apathy and multidomain cognitive/behavioral encephalopathy 20 days after the third teprotumumab infusion, with diffuse interictal epileptiform discharges on prolonged VEEG and prominent recovery after therapeutic plasma exchange (Naranjo score 6). The authors synthesize all published teprotumumab-associated encephalopathy cases and propose a three-hit pathogenic hypothesis centered on impaired IGF-1R neurotrophic signaling.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
